title: Black Line: Strong Work in Public
description: A positive practice instrument for concise, inspectable, revisable work. It reads self-declared tags and evidence labels against a versioned practice registry and returns one of four statuses over declaration coverage. It measures whether the evidence a practice asks for was declared — never whether the work is true, good, or permitted; an ALIGNED reading authorizes nothing. Subtitle: A Positive Operating Discipline for Concise, Rigorous Research and Engineering Code is MIT licensed; prose and figures are CC BY 4.0. See LICENSE in the repository.

methods.name: Versioned registry of eleven practices with coarse evidence labels
methods.description: Encodes practices such as question-first framing, source traceability, and clean reruns as 'wires', each with reviewed tags and required evidence labels.
methods.evidence: A versioned registry names eleven practices in six practice families, each with coarse review labels a collaborator could inspect.

methods.name: Staged evaluate_work evaluator returning four statuses
methods.description: Validates configuration and registry, then runs intake normalization, freshness partition, tag matching, and scoring to return ALIGNED, NEEDS_EVIDENCE, NEEDS_REWORK, or OUTSIDE_SCOPE.
methods.evidence: runs four stages — intake normalization, freshness partition, tag matching, and scoring with aggregation — and returns ALIGNED, NEEDS_EVIDENCE, NEEDS_REWORK, or OUTSIDE_SCOPE.

methods.name: Structural invariants tested against planted-bad registries
methods.description: Seven invariants check the registry's own shape, each demonstrated firing on a deliberately broken registry rather than only passing on the real one.
methods.evidence: Seven structural invariants check the registry’s own shape, and each is shown firing on a planted-bad registry rather than merely passing on the real one.

methods.name: Executed adversarial declarations against the real evaluator
methods.description: Runs label-stuffing, tag-minimization, and refresh-date laundering attacks to show how self-declared inputs can game the status.
methods.evidence: Because every input is self-declared, the instrument can be gamed by construction, and the honest response is to demonstrate the attacks rather than deny them. Each of the following was executed against the real evaluator.

methods.name: Three claim classes with distinct evidentiary burdens
methods.description: Separates implementation, methodological, and world/authority claims so that tests or citations do not silently change the type of claim made.
methods.evidence: The boundary becomes operational when claims are classified before they are written. Black Line distinguishes three burdens:

key_findings: An ALIGNED status only means every required label for each applicable practice was declared fresh, never that a source is real or a claim true.
Label-stuffing works: a research-tagged attempt declaring all 22 vocabulary labels with no artifacts returns ALIGNED.
Coverage is asymmetric: 27 of the 55 tag-practice cells are applicable, computed directly from the registry.
Seeded permutation sweeps confirm that once a declaration is non-empty the status never regresses, with the empty declaration as the intentional exception.
The author makes a design and implementation claim only; no user study or outcome comparison was run.
key_findings_evidence: An ALIGNED status means only that every required label for every applicable practice was declared as fresh under the chosen review date — never that a source is real or a claim is true.
The registry’s evidence vocabulary contains 22 distinct labels. A research-tagged attempt that simply declares all 22 — with no artifact behind any of them — returns ALIGNED.
Computed directly from the registry via coverage_matrix, 27 of the 55 tag-practice cells are applicable

seeded permutation sweeps over incremental declarations confirm that once a declaration is non-empty the status never regresses, with the empty-declaration boundary pinned as the one intentional exception

I am making a design and implementation claim, not an outcome claim. I have not run a user study, compared teams working with and without Black Line, or measured whether the practices improve correctness, speed, equity, or downstream decisions.

summary_provenance.method: Evidence-grounded extraction from full_text.md: every method and finding carries a verbatim quote from the paper text, mechanically verified to occur in full_text.md (whitespace/ligature-normalized) before merge.
summary_provenance.notes: Second work in the author's four-line set (Red/Black/Golden/White Line); findings are about the instrument's behaviour, not effects on work quality.
